description: Temporary Webmail session credentials (three of four pinned Session operations). Session-URL create_temp_user remains deferred under whm-api-client-8x0.1.33.

notes.text: Supplied strings retain case, punctuation and exact bytes and are encoded once. Optional null omits; empty strings remain supplied. No local locale, host, IP, password or name normalization or extra enum/range validation. One request only; no implicit lookup, login, redirect, retry, polling, cleanup or rollback. Live follow-up whm-api-client-8x0.2.69 remains OPEN.

Available from cPanel 86. Creates temporary credentials, not a Webmail login, session activity or mail access. Formal GET has x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none; effective transport is form POST on direct UAPI and WHM bridge. Login and remoteAddress are private inputs; password is sensitive where present.

The calling cPanel account must own the Webmail account. This authorized-owner operation does not verify the mailbox password; it is distinct from checkPassword and is never an automatic fallback after a password failure.

Lowercase locale is a server requirement; omitted locale uses the account locale. The pinned documentation describes remote_address as defaulting to the API caller IP and required for command-line use. That default does not establish WHM bridge inference; see the reviewed-build guidance below. The optional signature and null omission remain unchanged.

The source recipe requires a separate caller-controlled POST to https://<hostname>:2096<token>/login with session=<session> in the body. Null hostname means the server that answered the API; missing hostname remains omitted. This library does not construct, fetch or log in to that destination. Hostname/token/session combinations and returned Webmail URLs are private data. Optional hostname:string|null, session:string and token:string preserve omission, null hostname and empty or opaque credential bytes.

Reviewer seebeen reported on 2026-10-31 (review5725475353, original 5b005fb, cPanel 11.138.0.19) that all three Session creators succeeded as form POST on direct UAPI and WHM bridge with an explicit remoteAddress. Returned credentials were not used for login or access; non-null hostname remains unobserved. On that reviewed build, this method succeeded with remoteAddress omitted on direct UAPI but failed with an API error on WHM bridge; supply an explicit remoteAddress for the bridge on that build. This is scoped runtime evidence, not a universal route or authentication prohibition.

In the same reviewer suspended-mailbox case on 11.138.0.19, this non-password method still issued credentials on both routes while checkPassword refused. Login and access with those credentials were not tested; credential issuance establishes no suspension-enforcement or availability guarantee.
